title: Pristinia Homes & Households
dek: Homes, shared households and the changing claims through which adventurers make a place for themselves.

facts.Scope: Pristinian residential history with linked Prima comparisons
facts.Ownership: House-specific; not inferred from thread labels
facts.Record: Historical households, not a current occupancy register

sources: Fenumion_Housing_and_Scroll_Library_RP_History.md · supplied synthesis; quest evidence and explicit user canon take precedence
body:
Pristinia’s housing history records more than purchases. Homes become places of welcome, companionship, grief and shared routines. Occupancy, household membership and legal ownership can change at different times; an archive label does not resolve all three.

Alioth’s house and Magnus’s later claim

The supplied history identifies the property’s original introduction as Alioth’s house. Its early social life brings together visitors including Casimir, Wren, Draygar and Olokun. This is a history of a private home becoming a gathering place, not an assumption that visitors own it.

Magnus later occupies the house and says he has a deed. Farkur disputes that claim by referring to the town’s record of its owner. Pell’s later reported search lists Magnus as a Pristinian homeowner. That finding does not establish the exact transfer of this particular property or turn the newer thread name into its complete title history.

Wren’s promised refuge

Wren’s promise to give Olokun a place in her future home becomes a shared household: the account gives him a room and records her saying he lives there. Vaemyr’s later tour and relationship with Wren make the same home part of another developing bond.

The household’s social meaning changes as Olokun becomes uncomfortable remaining in what he jokes is their love nest and turns toward a home of his own. This is a domestic sequence, not a dated deed transfer or a claim that every earlier resident remains there now.

Different ways to make a home

Arjahn’s house is described through stone, a small garden, a modest guest room, a kitchen, a fireplace and space for training. Lucido’s account gives his home a quieter design: stone and First Forest wood, shoji doors and windows, a garden, sculpture and a lily pond. These choices add domestic context without replacing their quest histories with an invented personality.

Olokun’s home provides a place where friends talk before dangerous journeys. His joke about Pappy receiving it if he does not return is not a completed bequest. Pappy’s own home is remembered as a place someone can seek out because they trust him; its history does not establish a general public right of entry.

A shared domestic identity

The Lily Patch account explicitly identifies Di’trillio and Vessalia as co-owners. Decorating, books, flowers, crossing the threshold together and their first dance make the cottage their shared home. The history distinguishes that clear co-ownership from cases where another person is an important resident or visitor.

Precise addresses and the complete chronology of individual households remain unrecovered here. This residential guide does not assign every Prima house to one newly invented Pristinian neighbourhood.

Other Prima homes and institutions

Fenwick’s Wizarding Clock Tower belongs to Eovar and develops into the Silver Spire’s baths, market and healing house. It remains in its established geography. Coralyn’s Tideforged Depth is reported underwater off Eovar’s coast; Tshuka’s association does not by itself establish co-ownership. Greenbriar is described as a joint agricultural venture on the Eovar coast, with its full partner list unresolved.

Farkur’s Instant Fortress is remembered as a communal Ale-Chemy home base. That use belongs beside the organization’s later mobile and civic work; communal occupation does not settle the ownership of every resource.

Building rules and lived history

The Builder reference describes the current supplied homebrew requirements for construction. Those mechanics do not prove who built each historical house or when a project finished. The Scroll Library complements the housing record by preserving knowledge and civic records alongside the places people call home.

The Lily Patch cottage becomes a household

Di’trillio stocks the cottage and begins measuring a fence line. He and Vessalia share a meal made from his mother’s recipe and talk about learning to cook together. These small routines extend the earlier gift of a home. Their discussion of children remains a plan, not an established birth or marriage.
